Node.js and Express services, client-facing dashboards and admin panels,
shared component libraries documented in Storybook, end to end delivery
from design through deployment. TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, SQL.

APIs and service architecture: GraphQL and REST APIs in microservice
architectures, standardized response shapes and reusable middleware,
scalable schemas and consistent data contracts, pagination, filtering and
sorting over large datasets, role-based authorization with JWT and Clerk.

Performance and reliability: code splitting, lazy loading and render
optimization, TanStack Query caching and state management, Lighthouse and
Core Web Vitals measurement, structured logging with request correlation,
incident investigation down to root cause.

Cloud and AI in production: AWS Lambda, SQS and S3 with DynamoDB and
PostgreSQL, scheduled pipelines and pre-signed URL delivery, MCP servers
putting internal data inside the customer's Claude, OAuth with company,
sector and per-user entitlement checks, CI with Jenkins and SonarQube,
deploys on Vercel.

- 100,000+ students per district served by a scheduling platform, with

## Selected work

### Scheduling at scale
React, Node.js, GraphQL, AWS Lambda, SQS, S3, DynamoDB.

A full-stack scheduling system for an enterprise tutoring platform serving over
100,000 students per district. Scheduling errors fell 90%.

The interesting failure was report exports. Large districts produced datasets
big enough that the request timed out at API Gateway before the response
finished, and query tuning could not reach it because the gateway timeout is a
platform limit rather than a slow query. So exports left the request path
entirely. A cron job builds the report file every two hours and writes it to
S3, and the client receives a pre-signed URL instead of a payload. API Gateway
is no longer in the data path, which is what stopped report size from being an
availability problem.

Also built validation and consistency checks that block conflicting or
duplicate student assignments, plus an admin dashboard with downloadable
schedule summaries.

### Thirty unpaid teachers: an incident report
Node.js, AWS Lambda, DynamoDB, New Relic.

Around 4,500 teachers were due payment and about thirty were paid nothing:
their earnings attribute was never written, with no error anywhere. The trace
led to an update function that completed without writing. The real lesson was
that there was no process-level error capture, so the failure had nowhere to
land. Capture went in first; the next run revealed DynamoDB throttling writes
because the index's provisioned capacity was too low for payday load. The
thirty were paid manually, verified against the sheet, and the provisioning
was raised. The prevention that stayed: errors captured where they happen and
logs that mean something.

### AI in production for institutional investors
Next.js, Supabase, Trigger.dev, Claude Haiku, MCP.

Client work for Channel Dynamics, a market-intelligence platform for
institutional investors: the public site, the portal's analytics filtering,
and the observability wiring.

A weekly Trigger.dev job fans out into parallel tasks and compiles leadership
metrics into charts with one-line AI summaries, written by Claude Haiku on
purpose: one-liners do not need a frontier model. About a dozen leadership
inboxes, weekly.

A production MCP server, just launched, puts the published research inside
the customer's own Claude: seven tools to list, fetch, and semantically
search reports. Entitlements are the hard part: a company-level flag,
sector-level report entitlement, and per-user checks, with OAuth tied to the
customer's real account.

### Cutting first render in half
React, TanStack Query, code splitting.

Measured initial page load and Lighthouse on the routes users actually landed
on. The bundle shipped effectively the whole app on every route, so components
that only rendered below the fold were parsed before anything painted. Route
level code splitting, lazy loading, and rendering optimization took load from
3.5s to 1.8s and Lighthouse from 65 to 92.

A separate pass covered data fetching. The same queries were being refetched by
components mounting independently of each other. Moving to TanStack Query with
a deliberate cache and invalidation strategy cut redundant API requests 40% and
server load 20%.

### Shared component library
React, Tailwind, Chakra UI, shadcn/ui, Storybook.

Teams were rebuilding the same modal, form field and table. The cost was not
the duplicated code, it was that fixing one accessibility bug meant finding six
copies of it first. Consolidating those primitives into a documented shared
library made feature development cycles 30% faster and cut frontend code
duplication 20%.

## How I work

Services behind explicit API contracts. Standardized response shapes and
reusable middleware. Structured logging with request correlation, so an
incident starts from a query rather than a guess. End to end ownership from
design through deployment.
